summary: Nguyen Thi Xinh specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Punjabi University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Nguyen Van Hoa focuses on Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre (attested 2009).
Nguyen Van Thuong is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi under MA supervisor K. T. S. Sarao.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under Nordan Hutuktu, Gongga Rinpoche, Hsu Yun, Lianju Xia, and Jiaqi Wang. In Buddhist studies, he headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station and was a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.
Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Rissho University. He founded Nipponzan Myohoji and taught Gyoryo Maruyama.

Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama (1920–2001) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1976) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1976–1985), teaching David J. Kalupahana and Dhammanandā.

Nicholas J. Allen (1939–2020) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Rugby School and the University of Oxford (~1969–1976), he held posts at SOAS (1969–1971), Durham University (1972–1976), Oxford (~1976–2001), and Wolfson College, Oxford (~1976–2006).

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University (~1916–1921), he held posts there (~1925–1941), at academic institutes in Russia (1920–1941), and at the University of Washington (~1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts (~1893–1897) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1893–1898).
Nicholas Witkowski works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from Stanford University by 2015 and was a research fellow at the University of Tokyo (attested 2017).
Nicholson T. Collier works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicola Di Cosmo (born 1957) works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. Educated at Indiana State University and Indiana University, he held posts at Cambridge, Harvard, and Canterbury before joining the Institute for Advanced Study as professor in ~2003.
Nicolas Morrissey works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Gregory Schopen and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h, Peter Masefield, Kannika Wimonkasem, U-tain Wongsathit, Claudine Bautze-Picron, and Peter Skilling, also attending Silpakorn University, and was affiliated with Thammasat University in 2016.

Nicolas Tournadre (born 1959) is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology who studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Paris 8. He held posts at INALCO, LACITO, Paris 8, University of Virginia, University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She held posts at École du Louvre (~1946–1971), École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1958–1971), and INALCO (~1971–1976), and taught Heather Stoddard.

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian specialist. After studying in Copenhagen, Bonn, Paris, London, and Oxford, he became Professor of Indian-Oriental Philology at the University of Copenhagen in 1845.
Nigel Allan is a history and archaeology specialist who served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (attested 1993), succeeding Marianne Winder.

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) worked in history, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Calcutta and Leiden University, he held a post at Calcutta (~1937–1965) and served as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1965–1970).

Nika Jovic specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and was taught by Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008).
